docs.title: Ensembl Python project template
docs.text:
Ensembl Python project template documentation

This repository structure can be forked and used as the base template for developing a Python package (app or library). It contains boilerplate code and configuration for unit testing, linting, type checking, automatic documentation and CI/CD.

docs.title: How to install this library
docs.text: This Python library only requires Python 3.9+ to work.

docs.title: Basic installation
docs.text:
To install it, just run the following command:

pip3 install git+https://github.com/Ensembl/template-python.git

docs.title: Development-oriented installation
docs.text:
To perform a development installation it is advised to use a Python virtual environment (and activate it):

python3 -m venv path/to/virtual_env
source path/to/virtual_env/bin/activate

And then clone the GitHub repository and install it in edit mode:

git clone https://github.com/Ensembl/template-python.git
pip3 install -e template-python/.[cicd,doc]

The string you want to concatenate to "Hello ".

def hello(word: str) -> str:
    """Returns the concatenation of "Hello " with the given string.

    Args:
        word: The string you want to concatenate to "Hello ".

    """
    return f"Hello {word}"

def main() -> None:
    """Module's entry-point."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="Greetings program", description="Says 'hi' to the argument given")
    parser.add_argument("word")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    hello(args.word)
